requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Ordinary comments are excluded. Docstrings are source expressions and
participate in hashes along with the definition's other expressions.
rationale:
I judged the tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.sources.python.fingerprints`. I did not request implementation source. The obligations and their tests are below.

**SHA-256 over word-based structural encoding**
- `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` has a Python case (`def[f]`). It asserts the fingerprint value is 64 hex characters, which is the SHA-256 digest shape.
- It asserts that changing the whitespace in `"two words"` to `"two   words"` leaves the fingerprint unchanged.
- It asserts that `"twowords"` produces a different fingerprint, so words are hashed separately and whitespace is not hashed.
- The test does not pin a known digest value. The encoding is only specified as "unambiguous", so there is no exact expected digest to assert against. The length and hex check, together with the word-boundary assertions, is a reasonable check of the stated obligations.

**Fingerprint scheme**
- `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` checks Python with `check(languages::Python, "a.PYI", ...)`.
- It asserts `language.fingerprint_scheme()` and `L::default().fingerprint_scheme()` both equal `"python-structural-v1"`.
- It asserts the loaded `OutlineContent::fingerprint_scheme()` equals the language's scheme, which covers retention in loaded contents.
- It asserts the inferred and explicit outlines have equal fingerprints.

**Ordinary comments excluded**
- `src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]` has a Python case with a standalone `# note` and a trailing `# trailing`.
- Changing the comment text, or removing the comments entirely, leaves `node_hash` unchanged.
- Changing the non-comment word `x` to `y` changes the hash.
- The Python case in `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` repeats the comment-change check, combined with whitespace.

**Docstrings participate in the hash**
- The `docstring` assertions in `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` show that a docstring is hashed with the word rule.
- Changing whitespace inside the docstring leaves the fingerprint unchanged.
- Changing the docstring's words to `"changed words"` changes the fingerprint. This confirms docstrings are not excluded as comments.

**Related definition expressions (decorators)**
- `src/outline/tests.rs#fn[python_decorators_attach_to_the_decorated_definition_for_hashing]` shows that decorators are part of the definition's structural hash, and that blank lines and indentation changes are ignored. It also checks the class structural hash against its identity hash. This goes beyond what the subject strictly requires.

I found no untested obligation and no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Ordinary comments are excluded. Docstrings are source expressions and
participate in hashes along with the definition's other expressions.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
